title: Fourier methods and partial differential equations
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Solve representative heat, wave and Laplace equations with appropriate initial and boundary conditions.
primary_reading: MIT 18.152 Introduction to Partial Differential Equations

blocks.deliverable: Expand a piecewise function and discuss endpoint behavior.
Compute a transform and interpret frequency content.
Solve a finite interval diffusion problem.
Week 7 midterm; compare initial displacement and velocity roles.
Solve a rectangular domain problem and discuss uniqueness.
Check a Green function through its defining differential equation.
Submit convergence plots and an unseen methods final.

project: Solve a heat or wave boundary problem analytically and numerically and compare convergence.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major result aloud without notes.
